decisions.decision: Use a durable queue to buffer classification work
decisions.context: Millions of documents arrive each day, with strong seasonal volume swings. A queue lets ingestion absorb bursts while workers scale independently.
decisions.rationale: Buffering and independent worker scaling address variable load while keeping ingestion decoupled from slower LLM inference.
consequences: Track queue age and retry failed work.

decisions.context: Classification demand varies over the year, and the system must process millions of documents per day. Stateless workers can scale with queued demand.
decisions.rationale: A horizontally scaled pool can add throughput for seasonal peaks and reduce idle capacity outside them.
consequences: Worker scaling must respect LLM rate limits.
Define limits for backlog age and scale-up time.

decisions.context: Several teams consume classification results, so one processing workflow should serve multiple independent consumers. Events let teams consume results on their own schedules.
decisions.rationale: Events let teams consume the same classification independently without coupling classifier availability to each consumer.
consequences: Define and version a shared result schema.

decisions.decision: Version the classifier and record each prediction's version
decisions.context: Operators need to identify when classification quality drifts. Linking predictions to the model or prompt version makes quality changes traceable.
decisions.rationale: Version metadata makes it possible to compare quality across classifier changes and narrow the cause of observed drift.

decisions.decision: Monitor quality using labeled outcomes and drift indicators
decisions.context: Operators need to see when classification quality drifts, but production predictions alone do not establish correctness. Quality monitoring needs outcome labels when available, alongside changes in prediction patterns.

alternatives.label: Labeled outcome monitoring with drift indicators

chosen.label: Labeled outcome monitoring with drift indicators

decisions.rationale: Outcome labels provide a quality signal, while prediction-pattern indicators can alert operators before enough labels accumulate.
consequences: Define how labels are collected and joined to predictions.
